lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: There was a smash on Quay Street. All I saw was a shape by the glass, and then there wasn't.
lines.clause: a window went in at the shop on Quay Street and nobody saw more than a shape by the glass

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: Someone's put a window in down Quay Street. I caught a shape, and that's your lot from me.
lines.clause: somebody put a window in down Quay Street and all there was to see was a shape

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: Window's gone at the shop on Quay Street. I looked up, saw a shape move, and the glass was already down.
lines.clause: the window's gone at the shop on Quay Street and whoever did it was a shape and no more than that

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: Whoever did the window on Quay Street moved sharp, and there's something in the way he moves I'd know again.
lines.clause: the one that did the window on Quay Street had a way of moving that would be known again

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: I saw enough to know the walk on him. I'd pick it out in a crowd.
lines.clause: the man that put the window in had a walk that would be picked out in a crowd

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: The one that put the window in had a walk you'd know again. That's the one thing I'd swear to.
lines.clause: the fella that put the window in had a walk that would be known again

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: I got a proper look at him on Quay Street. I'd know that face again if he walked in here tomorrow.
lines.clause: whoever broke the shop window on Quay Street showed his face, and that face is known now

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: He looked straight at me. Couldn't tell you his name, but I've got his face now.
lines.clause: the man that did the window looked straight at the one who saw him, and his face is known if not his name

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: Saw him full in the face when the glass went. I'd know him again anywhere, whoever he turns out to be.
lines.clause: the one that smashed the shop window on Quay Street was seen full in the face and would be known again anywhere

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: It was Nowak that put the window in on Quay Street, plain as day. The new owner up at Mickey's, no mistaking him.
lines.clause: it was Nowak that put the window in on Quay Street, the new owner up at Mickey's, and there's no mistaking him

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: That was the new owner, the one that's got Mickey's now. Nowak. I'd know him anywhere.
lines.clause: the new owner that's got Mickey's now, Nowak, put the window in, and he'd be known anywhere

lines.speaker: w1
lines.text: Nowak did it, the fella from Mickey's. Saw him clear as I see you, and I know exactly who he is.
lines.clause: the fella from Mickey's put the shop window in, Nowak, and he was seen clear enough that there's no question who he is

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A shape, that's the whole of it? Whoever it was picked a wet night to be nobody in particular.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A shape's not much to go on. Half the town could pass for that on a night like this.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: Just a shape, you say. Could've been the tide walking, for all that tells anyone.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A donkey jacket's not a face. That's half the harbour's wardrobe you've described.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A limp and a cap. Half the dock front walks like that at the end of a shift.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A pale mac with the collar up. That's every second man on a wet street, that is.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: You'd know him again, that's something. Next time that face shows, you sing out.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: A face you'd know is worth more than most talk in here. Keep it in mind.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: If you'd know him again, that's more than the coppers usually get told round here.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: Nowak, is it. The new owner's making a name for himself, and not the one Mickey'd have wanted.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: That's the new owner, that. Word'll be round the Hook before the glass is swept up.

lines.speaker: n2
lines.text: Nowak and a broken window on Quay Street. That'll travel faster than the tide does.
